- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and price is rising, model may lag; adjust forecast upward slightly to capture momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.11), model often overfits recent volatility; use 18-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
- If true outcome shows early downward correction after forecast peak, model may be too optimistic; reduce peak forecast by 1–3% and shift trough earlier.
